task.description:
ELIXIR-DEV implemented REQ-197 against lib/letflow/design/req197-expr-arithmetic-and-errors.md, extending lib/letflow/engine/expr.ex only (no other file touched -- confirmed by `git status --short`: only lib/letflow/engine/expr.ex is modified). Added: the 5 new arith_op() binary operators plus unary negation as new ast() node shapes ({:arith, op, l, r}, {:neg, ast}); 2 new precedence levels (parse_additive/parse_multiplicative/parse_unary inserted between parse_cmp and the renamed parse_primary, per design §2.1/§3.1); the int/float promotion + div/mod-by-zero + null-first arithmetic semantics (design §4.2/§4.3); the deliberate null-in-comparison-vs-null-in-arithmetic asymmetry via a new nil-check guard inserted ahead of the existing is_number guard in the ordering-comparison clause (originally expr.ex:437-446); and a new parse_strict/1 entry point returning a structured parse_failure() (line/column/token_text/message).

THREE ITEMS EXPLICITLY FLAGGED FOR REVIEWER (do not let any of these get silently accepted or silently expanded without an explicit REVIEWER decision):

(a) OQ-1 DEFERRAL (design §4.3/§4.6, design doc §12) -- BLOCKING per the Step 2a handoff's own gating instruction. The full signed-infinity/NaN 3-way split (:infinity | :neg_infinity | :nan) for float division/modulo by zero was NOT implemented, because it could not be verified against R-Co's real src/expr/evaluator.zig (no *.zig file reachable on this host) and has zero AC test coverage. Instead, the design's own stated SAFE FALLBACK was implemented: a single unsigned `:infinity` marker (type `infinity_marker :: :infinity`, see the @typedoc directly above it in expr.ex, which states this gate explicitly) for float division by a zero divisor (any dividend, including 0.0/0.0) and for `:infinity` participating in ordering comparisons as the greatest possible value. Float modulo by zero is always an error (`{:modulo_by_zero, :float, l, r}`), per the requirement text and design table, with no infinity/NaN sentinel involved. THIS SATISFIES AC4's literal wording ('float division by zero produces infinity') but does NOT implement the negative-dividend-to-negative-infinity or 0.0/0.0-to-NaN cases the design's own §4.3 reasoned extension describes. REVIEWER must explicitly decide: accept this unsigned-only fallback as REQ-197's final shape, or request the fuller 3-way signed/NaN design (which would need its own follow-up implementation pass plus new AC-level test coverage, since none exists today).

(b) OQ-4 (design §4.3 row A, §12) -- AWARENESS ONLY, NOT BLOCKING. Negative-operand integer division/modulo (e.g. -7/2, -7 % 2) uses Elixir's native `div/2`/`rem/2` semantics directly (truncate-toward-zero, result sign follows the dividend for `rem/2`) with no new type/AST surface. This is the design's own reasoned choice, not independently verified against R-Co's real evaluator.zig, and no acceptance criterion exercises a negative-operand case. No action requested beyond REVIEWER's awareness that this is an unverified-but-low-risk assumption a future R-Co-source-access audit should confirm.

(c) REAL BEHAVIOUR CHANGE TO EXISTING CODE (design §4.5, REVISED rework iteration 1) -- the ordering-comparison clause (`<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`; originally expr.ex:437-446) now returns `{:ok, nil}` when either operand is `nil`, checked in a new guard inserted immediately ahead of the pre-existing `is_number(lv) and is_number(rv)` guard. Before this change, a nil operand in an ordering comparison produced `{:error, {:eval_error, {:type_mismatch, op, lv, rv}}}`; the new behaviour propagates nil as a real (non-error) value instead. CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR already confirmed (Step 1b re-check, see handoffs/WF02-REQ197-20260830/step-01b-code-design-validator.json) that test/letflow/engine/expr_test.exs has zero existing nil/null test coverage to break, and this is required by AC5's own wording (the two-different-eval/2-outcomes asymmetry). Flagged here per this role's own instruction not to silently proceed on a load-bearing 'unchanged' claim -- this specific clause IS changed, deliberately, and evaluate_condition/2's own external behaviour is unaffected (its unconditional `else _ -> false` composition still treats a non-`true` eval/2 result, including `{:ok, nil}`, as `false`).

ADDITIONAL IMPLEMENTATION NOTE (not a security concern, flagged for REVIEWER's OTP-idiom/code-quality pass rather than SECURITY-REVIEWER's gate, but included here since this handoff routes through SECURITY-REVIEWER first): parse_strict/1 was given its OWN position-tracking tokenizer/parser pair (tokenize_positioned/1, do_tokenize_positioned/4, parse_or_p/2..parse_primary_p/2), structurally mirroring the existing tokenize/1+parse_or/1..parse_primary/1 pair one-for-one, rather than threading position bookkeeping through the single existing implementation as design doc §6.2 states as its preference ('share one underlying tokenizer and one underlying grammar implementation'). This was a deliberate, lower-risk choice to avoid touching the existing tokenizer's delicate escape-handling code (which carries two prior bug-fix histories, ISS-0086/ISS-0087) and to guarantee parse/1's outer shape and internal test-observable behaviour stay byte-for-byte safe. `parse/1`'s own @spec, outer return shape, and evaluate_condition/2's source are unedited -- confirmed by direct review during implementation and by the two required test files passing unmodified. Noted as a design-preference deviation, not a scope or AC violation, for REVIEWER's awareness.

No tenant-data path is touched: expr.ex remains a pure module (no Letflow.Repo, no Logger, no clock, no :rand/:crypto, no File/HTTP) -- the moduledoc's own purity grep (quoted below) returns zero matches, same as before this requirement. No migration, no API route, no secret handling changed.

result.summary:
SECURITY-REVIEWER gate on REQ-197 (lib/letflow/engine/expr.ex) -- PASS. Ran own scope test rather than trusting the ORCH/ELIXIR-DEV note: `git diff main...HEAD --stat` confirms only lib/letflow/engine/expr.ex is touched in production code (plus the design doc, test files, and handoff/status/registry bookkeeping) -- no migration, no route, no secret-resolution code. Re-ran the purity grep myself against the real current file (not the report): zero matches, exit 1. Full findings, including the two substantive checks below, written to handoffs/WF02-REQ197-20260830/security-review-req197-findings.md (H6: filename does not start with 'step').

INV-1..INV-8: INV-8 (no unhandled crashes) APPLIES and PASSES -- verified both int and float division/modulo-by-zero clauses are ordered ahead of the native div/rem//ArithmeticError-raising clauses (expr.ex:1072-1093), and apply_neg/1 is exhaustive over nil/:infinity/number/catch-all. INV-1/2/3/4/5/6/7 all NOT-APPLICABLE -- expr.ex is a pure function over a caller-supplied variables map, no Repo/SQL/secrets/response-shaping/lookup-by-ID anywhere in this diff.

Point 3 (parse_strict/1 error surface): traced mk_err/4 -> package_failure/1 -> describe_parse_error/1 (expr.ex:489-510). token_text is always a substring of the caller's own input captured during tokenization; message is one of 8 fixed English sentences with no interpolation of the reason payload's internal structure. No stack trace, no internal state, no cross-tenant data ever enters a parse_failure(). Also confirmed evaluate_condition/2's call graph (translate_cel_to_expr/1 -> parse/1 -> eval/2) never calls parse_strict/1 -- inert on the gateway-evaluation path today. Safe.

Point 4 (nil-propagation-through-comparison bypass): read transition.ex:660-676 (evaluate_conditioned_edges -> `if Expr.evaluate_condition(edge.condition, variables)`) and evaluate_condition/2 itself (expr.ex:1146-1155), which pattern-matches literally `{:ok, true}` via `with`, `else _ -> false` otherwise. The new nil-propagation path produces `{:ok, nil}`, which does not match `{:ok, true}` and falls to `false` -- identical external outcome to the pre-change `{:error, {:eval_error, {:type_mismatch, ...}}}` path it replaced (also caught by `else _ -> false`). No route exists by which nil-propagation can flip an exclusive-gateway branch to true. Change is textually scoped to `<`/`<=`/`>`/`>=` only (expr.ex:1005 guard), `==`/`!=` untouched. No bypass.

Point 5 (unsigned-:infinity fallback, OQ-1): apply_float_arith(:div, _l, r) when r == 0.0 (expr.ex:1088) collapses every float division by zero to the same unsigned :infinity marker regardless of dividend sign, and apply_ordering/3 treats :infinity as the greatest possible value in every comparison. Concretely demonstrated (not just hypothesized): a gateway condition of the form `amount / 0.0 > threshold` evaluates true for both a large positive AND a large-magnitude negative amount, where a signed-infinity implementation would put the negative case at -infinity (false for any finite positive threshold) -- a real, demonstrable gateway-decision divergence, not a display nuance. This does NOT cross any INV-1..INV-8 boundary (single tenant's own process definition producing a wrong-but-internally-consistent decision on that tenant's own data -- no cross-tenant leakage, no secret exposure, no crash, no SQL/auth bypass), so it is correctly modeled as an open design question rather than a BLOCKER here. Carried forward to REVIEWER with the concrete exploit shape spelled out, since 'not obviously a vulnerability' undersold how demonstrable the divergence is.

All three ELIXIR-DEV-flagged items -- OQ-1 sign-off (with the concrete finding above), OQ-4 awareness, and the parse_strict/1 tokenizer-duplication design-preference deviation -- are carried forward explicitly to REVIEWER in step-02d.
